source: Owner instruction 2026-11-25: two NVIDIA keys today, more later; one key serves one worker, and a session that handled several roles can be split into two.
note: The key roster. It names where each credential lives and which model a worker runs on; it never holds a key. The credential is read by the provider configuration from a file or an environment variable outside this repository, so no agent ever sees the secret.
rules: One key serves one worker process: the worker is started with the slot's model, so two workers can run at the same time on two keys.
Adding a key means adding one provider entry, one slot row, and one more dispatcher; no lane code changes.
The owner places the key file; no agent reads, prints, copies, or asks for the secret.
Two keys from one NVIDIA account are not two accounts: each key's own quota and the provider's terms apply, so a slot stays inside its key's documented limit.
